Hmm, the last thing in that thread is Bob saying this (see below).  That all works for me.  I really don't like calling it fabs as it is not user-friendly.
A


I think we should go 180 on this and instead add the following signatures 
with obvious definitions: 

  real abs(real); 

  real max(real,real); 
  real max(real, int); 
  real max(int, real); 

We already have: 

  int abs(int); 
  int max(int, int); 

Is that OK with everyone?   

Do we deprecate and eventually get rid of the f versions?  I don't see 
the point of keeping them.  I don't really see anyone wanting to do 
fabs(int,int), which is all we'd be losing.  Anywhere you can use a real 
value in Stan you can use an int.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] abs and fabs
parts:
I can take another look at that. We've followed the easy path
of mirroring the C++ design. To remind everyone of the issue,
in C++, fabs() has a single signature (actually it includes parallel
versions for float and long double, but this is the only relevant one)

double fabs(double);

whereas abs() has two signatures

double abs(double);
int abs(int);

When you combine this with the way promotion from integers to
real (floating point) numbers works in C++ and in Stan, what you
get is this:

abs(int) : int
abs(real) : real

fabs(int) : real
fabs(real) : real

The result type is different for integer arguments. All the functions
we have vectorized (like log and exp and sqrt) behave like fabs --- they
always return real values, even if the argument is an integer.

We could deprecate fabs() and either

* forego vectorizing abs(), or

* we could implement a one-off non-standard vectorization for abs
that would return integers when given integer arguments

What we can't do is just decide to have abs return real values for
integer inputs---that'd mess up programs.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] abs and fabs
parts:
Bob,

I defer to you on this. If fabs is the way to go, it's the way to go, and then we just need something in the manual explaining why. I agree that it would be weird to have both abs and fabs if they do different things. I also think vectorization is important for user-friendliness. Indeed, in my opinion, the user-friendliness of vectorization outweighs the un-user-friendliness of abs.

The larger issue, I think, is that the integer/real distinction causes problems all over the place in Stan. It's unavoidable, perhaps, but still annoying. The example that keeps coming up is when I switch from linear regression to logistic. With linear I have vector[N] y; and with logistic I have int y[N]. It's becoming less of a problem for me because I've been trying to consistently use the "long" format for regression data, but when I had data such as y[i,j] and was using to_vector(), it was kind of annoying.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] abs and fabs
parts:
I think we can give you the behavior you want without
confusing the relation between Stan and C++. I don't
think Stan programmers are going to need the fabs version
that applies to an integer and returns a real value.

It's just more work to vectorize abs because it doesn't
have the right signature.

We'll still be able to keep fabs() in the math library.

I can prioritize getting this change in. I reopened
the issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1255

- Bob
